title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent user (EE1) shares personal identifying information (PII) including email, password, name, government ID, and six-digit code with the Authentication Service (P1). This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to an untrusted third party.
assumptions: The parent user intends to register and expects the service to process the data for authentication purposes.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The Authentication Service (P1) receives the PII from EE1 and stores it in a way that causes the threat. This includes storing the data in a database or system where it can be accessed by unauthorized parties or used for purposes other than authentication.
assumptions: The service assumes it has the necessary permissions to store and process this data.

title: Account Information Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P1) shares parent account information with the data store (DS1) without verifying the recipient's identity or authorization. This allows unauthorized access to sensitive account data.

title: Data Processing for Unauthorized Access
description: The destination element (MongoDB collection DS1) receives the parent account data and stores it in a way that allows for unauthorized access or processing by unauthorized parties.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P1) shares JWT tokens and user data with the parent element (ExternalEntity EE1). This act of sharing causes the threat because the parent entity may use this data to identify or link the user to other entities, violating privacy principles.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: The source element (Process P1) shares JWT tokens and user data with the parent element (ExternalEntity EE1). This act of sharing causes the threat because the parent entity may modify or tamper with the data in transit, violating data integrity principles.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The external entity (EE2) shares its identity (email) with the authentication service (P1) without any authentication or authorization mechanism. This allows P1 to identify and potentially track the user.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: The external entity (EE2) shares its password (a sensitive credential) with the authentication service (P1). This exposes the user's authentication credentials to the service.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: The authentication service (P1) receives the user's credentials and may use them to access other parts of the system or for unauthorized access to the user's account.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P1) shares JWT (userType child) data with the Child User (ExternalEntity EE2). This act of sharing causes the threat because the JWT contains sensitive user identity information (userType) that is transmitted to an external entity without appropriate access controls or encryption.

title: Data Linking/Identification
description: The data flow (DF5) transmits JWT (userType child) data in transit. This data-centric threat arises because the JWT contains user identity information (userType) that can be used to link or identify the parties involved in the flow, potentially compromising privacy if the data is intercepted or misused.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (Child User EE2) receives the JWT (userType child) data. This destination-centric threat arises because the recipient may process or store the user identity information in a way that causes the threat, such as storing it in a database without proper access controls or encryption.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: External entity (EE1) shares personal data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) with the profile management process (P3) without explicit consent or a valid legal basis for processing.

title: Data Processing for Profiling
description: The profile management process (P3) receives and stores the personal data, enabling the creation of a profile which may be used for profiling or targeted advertising.

title: Child Profile Data Exposure
description: The source element (Process P3) shares the child profile data (id P3) with the data store (DS2) without any explicit consent or authorization from the parent entity. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to unauthorized access.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (MongoDB collection DS2) receives the child profile data and processes or stores it in a way that causes the threat. The system may store the data in a way that allows for future unauthorized access or modification by unauthorized parties.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: External entity EE2 (Child User) shares personal identity information (e.g., name, email, ID) with the Video Management Service (P2) during the request phase.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: EE2 shares sensitive video metadata (e.g., video ID, thumbnail, duration) with P2, which may be used to identify the user or infer their viewing habits.

title: Data Processing for Inference
description: P2 processes the received video data (e.g., extracts video ID, duration, thumbnail) to perform the search, which enables inference about the user's viewing behavior and preferences.

title: User Profile Inconsistency
description: P2 may update the user's profile with new video data (e.g., new likes, comments) without verifying the authenticity of the data or the user's intent, leading to profile inconsistencies.

title: Metadata Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares video metadata (e.g., file paths, timestamps, user IDs) with the data flow, which can be used to identify the specific user or link to their video content.
assumptions: The process does not encrypt or obfuscate the metadata before transmission.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow (DF9) transmits metadata about the parties involved (e.g., user ID, video file path) in transit. This allows an attacker to correlate the video content with the user's identity, enabling targeted profiling or tracking.
assumptions: The metadata is not encrypted or obfuscated during transmission.

title: Unrestricted Access to Video Files
description: The destination element (MongoDB collection DS3) receives the video files and metadata. Without appropriate access controls, the destination can access, download, or exfiltrate the video content, violating user privacy.
assumptions: The destination does not enforce strict access controls or encryption for video files.

title: Child Search History Exposure
description: The source element (Process P3) shares its internal state (child search and watch history) with the data store (DS2) without any explicit consent or encryption. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to the destination element.
assumptions: The process does not encrypt the search history before sharing.

title: Child Search History Processing
description: The destination element (MongoDB collection DS2) receives the child search and watch history and processes it. This action causes the threat because the data is stored in a way that allows for potential linkage or identification of the child based on the search history.
assumptions: The database does not apply any additional anonymization or masking to the search history.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Data
description: External entity EE1 (Parent User) shares video data with Video Management Service P2 without explicit consent or authorization, potentially exposing sensitive content.

title: Data Processing and Storage Risks
description: Video Management Service P2 processes and stores the uploaded video data, which may be used for profiling or targeted advertising without proper data minimization or user consent.

title: Unauthorized Video Sharing
description: The source element (Process P2) shares video data without explicit, granular consent from the Child User (EE2). This allows the data to be accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow (DF12) transmits video data in a way that allows the source (P2) and destination (EE2) to be linked or identified by metadata (e.g., user ID, video hash) that could be used to track or profile the parties involved.

title: Inappropriate Data Processing
description: The destination element (Child User EE2) receives the video data and processes it in a way that causes privacy risks, such as storing it in a way that enables future profiling or linking to other data sources.

title: Data Collection
description: The source element (DataStore) actively collects browsing data from the child profiles collection, which inherently exposes sensitive user data to the system.
assumptions: The child profiles collection contains unfiltered or partially filtered browsing data.

title: Data Linking
description: The data flow itself carries metadata about the parties involved (e.g., user ID, device ID, IP address) that can be used to link or identify the source data with the destination data.
assumptions: The data flow carries standard metadata fields (e.g., user_id, device_id) that are not encrypted or obfuscated.

title: Data Processing
description: The destination element (AI Recommendation Engine) processes the received data, which may involve training models or generating recommendations based on the browsing data, potentially leading to re-identification or inference of sensitive information.
assumptions: The AI model is trained on the collected browsing data, and the output recommendations may be used for personalization.

title: Data Collection
description: The process P4 collects browsing data from users without explicit, informed consent from the user.
assumptions: Users are unaware of the specific browsing data being collected.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific browsing data is considered sensitive personal information under applicable regulations.

title: Data Processing
description: The process P4 processes the collected browsing data to generate AI recommendations.
assumptions: The processing involves analyzing user behavior patterns.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific browsing data is considered sensitive personal information under applicable regulations.

title: Data Usage
description: The process P4 uses the browsing data to make AI recommendations to users.
assumptions: The AI model is trained on historical data that may not be representative of current user behavior.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific browsing data is considered sensitive personal information under applicable regulations.

title: Data Sharing
description: The process P4 shares the browsing data with Third-Party Advertisers (EE3).
assumptions: The sharing is necessary for the advertising service to function.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific browsing data is considered sensitive personal information under applicable regulations.

title: Data In Transit
description: Browsing data is transmitted over the network to EE3.
assumptions: The data is encrypted during transmission.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific browsing data is considered sensitive personal information under applicable regulations.

title: Data In Transit
description: Browsing data is transmitted over the network to EE3.
assumptions: The data is encrypted during transmission.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific browsing data is considered sensitive personal information under applicable regulations.

title: Data Processing
description: The third-party advertiser processes the browsing data to generate advertising impressions.
assumptions: The advertiser uses the data to target ads to users.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific browsing data is considered sensitive personal information under applicable regulations.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: The source element (Process P1) shares government ID images with the data store (DS4). This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is transferred to a location where it may be accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Access or Processing
description: The destination element (DataStore DS4) receives the government ID images. The threat arises because the recipient may store, process, or disseminate this data in ways that cause privacy violations.

title: JWT Expiration
description: The JWT stored in localStorage may expire before the browser session ends, causing the authentication to fail.

title: JWT Storage
description: The JWT is stored in localStorage, which is a client-side storage mechanism. This is a sensitive storage location.

title: JWT Access
description: The browser (destination) accesses the JWT from localStorage, potentially exposing it to unauthorized access.

title: Child Profile Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P3) shares the child profile data with the parent User (ExternalEntity EE1) without verifying the parent's identity or authorization to access the specific child records.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF17) transmits child profile data to the parent User. The parent's identity is not explicitly verified at the source, and the data flow itself may be used to link or identify the parent-user relationship, creating a data-centric threat.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (ExternalEntity EE1) receives the child profile data and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat, such as storing the data in a way that allows future unauthorized access or linking to other user profiles.
